parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows the market for sugar in Singapore with an equilibrium point of X.

![Supply and demand graph showing shifts. Supply lines S1, S2, S3 intersect demand lines D1, D2, D3 at points A, B, C, X, and D. Axes labeled price and quantity.](assets/001-supply-and-demand-graph-showing-shifts-supply-li.png)

Which point represents the new equilibrium after the government legislates that fizzy drinks have to halve their sugar content and two of the three sugar manufacturers decide to leave the market?
parts.solution_md:
**D is correct** as the government legislation will cause the demand for sugar by fizzy drink manufacturers to decrease (shift left D1 to D2). At the same time sugar manufacturers leave the market causing the supply curve to shift left from S1 to S2

- A is incorrect as the demand for sugar decreases, it does not shift right
- B is incorrect as the demand for sugar decreases, it does not shift right
- C is incorrect as the supply of sugar decreases, it shifts left

parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows the global market for copper with an equilibrium point of X.

![Supply and demand graph showing shifts. Supply lines S1, S2, S3 intersect demand lines D1, D2, D3 at points A, B, C, X, and D. Axes labeled price and quantity.](assets/001-supply-and-demand-graph-showing-shifts-supply-li.png)

Which point represents the new equilibrium after the copper producers’ costs increase and there is rapid global economic growth?
parts.solution_md:
**A is correct **as the increase in costs shifts the supply curve from S1 to S2. At the same time global economic growth leads to an increase in demand from D1 to D2 leading to a new equilibrium at point A

- B is incorrect as an increase in costs does not shift the supply curve right
- C is incorrect as rapid global growth does not shift the demand curve left
- D is incorrect as rapid global growth does not shift the demand curve left

parts.problem_md:
In 2015, the world price of oil fell rapidly due to changes in the conditions of demand and supply. One change was the use of a new method of extraction called fracking.

Which event would **not** have contributed to the fall in prices?
parts.solution_md:
**C is correct** as the prevention of fracking projects would limit supply, leading to an increase in prices

- A is incorrect as falling demand from China would have contributed to excess supply and lower prices
- B is incorrect as increased supply from Saudi Arabia would have contributed to excess supply and lower prices
- D is incorrect as increased domestic supply in the USA would have contributed to global excess supply leading to a fall in prices

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: China’s growth slowed leading to lower oil imports.

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: Saudi Arabia increased the volume of its oil supplies.

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: UK protest groups prevented the introduction of fracking projects.

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: USA became more self-sufficient in oil due to fracking and reduced imports.

parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows the market for a firm making electric vehicles with an initial equilibrium at X.

![nov-2018-v2qp-p1-cie-eco-q5](assets/002-nov-2018-v2qp-p1-cie-eco-q5.png)

What will be the new equilibrium if there is an increase in the government subsidy for electric vehicles and a 40% increase in the cost of petrol?
parts.solution_md:
**C is correct **as the government subsidy will cause the supply curve for electric vehicles to shift right from S<sub>1</sub> to S<sub>3</sub>. At the same time , the demand for the substitute (petrol cars) will decrease due to the increased price of petrol and some consumers will choose to purchase an electric vehicle instead - this will shift the demand curve for electric vehicles from D<sub>1</sub> to D<sub>3</sub> resulting in a new equilibrium at point C

- A is incorrect as the the supply increases
- B is incorrect as the supply increases, it does not decrease (shift left)
- D is incorrect as the demand increases, it does not decrease (shift left)

parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows the market for a firm making clothing with an initial equilibrium of X.

![nov-2018-v2qp-p1-cie-eco-q5](assets/002-nov-2018-v2qp-p1-cie-eco-q5.png)

What will be the new equilibrium if there is a successful advertising campaign by a rival firm and an increase in workers’ wages?
parts.solution_md:
A is correct as the increase in workers wages (costs) shifts the supply curve from S1 to S2. At the same a successful advertising campaign by a competitor leads to a decrease in demand from D1 to D2 leading to a new equilibrium at point A

- B is incorrect as a successful advertising campaign by a competitor does not increase demand
- C is incorrect as the increase in workers wages (costs) shifts the supply curve left, not right
- D is incorrect as the increase in workers wages (costs) shifts the supply curve left, not right

parts.problem_md:
A large amount of the agricultural products in a country were damaged by floods. What is likely to have happened to the price of agricultural products and the volume of imports of agricultural products? | | price of products | volume of imports | |---|---|---| | **A**

**B**

**C**

**D** | fall

fall

rise

rise | fall

rise

fall

rise |
parts.solution_md:
**D is correct **as a shortage always raises the price and imports are a key way of meeting a shortage - so imports will increase

- A is incorrect as both will rise
- B is incorrect prices will rise due to the shortage
- C is incorrect as imports will rise to meet the demand

parts.problem_md: If consumer incomes increase, what effect might this have on the equilibrium price and quantity of cinema tickets?
parts.solution_md:
- C is correct as the demand for cinema tickets will shift right (it is a normal good) leading to an increase in price and quantity in the market

  - A is incorrect as the equilibrium quantity will increase
  - B is incorrect as the equilibrium price will increase
  - D is incorrect as the equilibrium price will increase

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: Equilibrium price increases, equilibrium quantity decreases

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: Equilibrium price decreases, equilibrium quantity decreases

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: Equilibrium price increases, equilibrium quantity increases

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: Equilibrium price remains unchanged, equilibrium quantity increases

parts.problem_md: What happens to the market for umbrellas when it starts raining?
parts.solution_md:
- B is correct as demand will shift right at every price level - this is a form of an increase in seasonal demand

  - A is incorrect as demand will shift right, not left
  - C is incorrect as the supply curve will not shift
  - D is incorrect as the supply curve will not shift

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: Demand decreases

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: Demand increases

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: Supply decreases

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: Supply increases

parts.problem_md: Suppose the price of a complementary good decreases. How would this likely affect the equilibrium price and quantity of the main product?
parts.solution_md:
- B is correct as the demand for the main product will shift right (e.g printers) as the complementary product (printer ink) is now cheaper - leading to an increase in price and quantity in the market

  - A is incorrect as the equilibrium quantity will increase
  - C is incorrect as the equilibrium price will increase
  - D is incorrect as the equilibrium price and quantity will increase

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: Equilibrium price would increase, quantity would decrease

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: Equilibrium price and quantity would both increase

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: Equilibrium price would decrease, quantity would increase

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: Equilibrium price and quantity would both decrease

parts.problem_md: If a technological advancement reduces the cost of production for a product, what is likely to happen to its equilibrium price and quantity?
parts.solution_md:
- C is correct as the supply for the product will shift right leading to an decrease in price and and an increase in the quantity in the market

  - A is incorrect as the equilibrium quantity will increase
  - B is incorrect as the equilibrium quantity will increase
  - D is incorrect as the equilibrium price will decrease

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: Equilibrium price decreases, quantity decreases

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: Equilibrium price increases, quantity decreases

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: Equilibrium price decreases, quantity increases

choices.label: D

  - B is incorrect as the quantity in the market increases

  - D is incorrect as the equilibrium price will decrease, not increase

  - D is incorrect as the equilibrium price will increase, not decrease

parts.problem_md:
In 2018 the UK government introduced a tax on the production of sugary drinks. How would this affect the market for sugary drinks as shown on a demand and supply diagram? | | demand curve for sugary drinks | supply curve of sugary drinks | |---|---|---| | **A**

**B**

**C**

**D** | contraction in demand

extension in demand

shift to the left

shift to the right | shift to the left

shift to the right

contraction in supply

extension in supply |
parts.solution_md:
A is correct as the tax will shift the supply curve to the left resulting in a movement (contraction) along the demand curve

- B is incorrect as a tax does not increase production (shift of supply to the right)
- C is incorrect as the imposition of a tax is a supply side issue and will not shift the demand curve
- D is incorrect as the imposition of a tax is a supply side issue and will not shift the demand curve

parts.problem_md:
In 2019 the Malaysian government increased a per litre subsidy on the production of petrol. How would this affect the market for petrol as shown on a demand and supply diagram? | | demand curve for petrol | supply curve of petrol | |---|---|---| | **A**

**B**

**C**

**D** | extension in demand

contraction in demand

shift to the left

shift to the right | shift to the right

shift to the left

contraction in supply

extension in supply |
parts.solution_md:
- **A is correct **as the subsidy will shift the supply curve to the right resulting in a movement (extension) along the demand curve to the right

  - B is incorrect as the supply curve will shift to the right
  - C is incorrect as there is an extension in demand to the right - not a shift to the left
  - D is incorrect as there is an extension in demand to the right - not a shift to the right
